verses.1: And many days passed. Then God spoke to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go to Ahazib and give him a grain offering on the face of the land.”
verses.2: And Elisha went to see Ahah. Hunger was very severe in Shomron.
verses.3: And Ahau called out to Obed-Ehuda, who was sitting on the roof. Obed-Ehuda feared Jehovah greatly.
verses.4: And in Kiryat, Eizbel gathered the prophets of Jehovah. He took one hundred of His servants and hid them in a cave. Fifty of them were given bread and water to eat.
verses.5: And Ahava said to Obadiah, “Go into the land and explore all the rivers and streams. If you find some pastureland, where you can raise cattle and sheep, then you may live there.” But if you don’t find any such place, then you must go elsewhere.
verses.6: And they were given land to pass through. Aba went along one path alone, and Obedyehu went along another path alone.
verses.7: And Hezekiah went along the road. Then Eliyah called out to him. Hezekiah recognized him and fell on his face. He said, “You are my Lord, Eliyah.”
verses.8: And he said to him, “I will go and tell your master, ‘Here I am.’”
verses.9: And he said, “What is my sin? That you give your servant into the hands of Ahab, so that he may kill me.”
verses.10: May the LORD your God live! If there is a nation or kingdom where no one has gone to ask for you, and they say, “We will take over the kingdom and the nation,” then we will not find them there.
verses.11: And now, you shall say to your master: “Look, Eliyahu.”
verses.12: And I will go from you. The Spirit of the LORD will carry you away, even though I don’t know where. I will go to tell Ahab, but he won’t find you. Then I will kill him, and your servant will fear the LORD more than his own son.
verses.13: I did not tell my master about what I had done in the valley of Izbel. I buried all of the prophets of Jehovah there. There were a hundred and fifty men who were buried there. I fed them with bread and water.
verses.14: And now, you shall say to your master: “Look, Elijah is here; he will kill me.”
verses.15: And Elyahhu said, “May the Lord, whose army I have stood before Him, live! For today I will see Him.”
verses.16: And Obed-Edom went to see Ahau. He reported to him. Then Ahau went to see Eliyah.
verses.17: And Ahava saw Elihu, and he said to him, “You are this Israel’s leader.”
verses.18: And he said, “I have not abandoned Israel. It is only you and your family who have abandoned the commandments of Jehovah and gone after other men.”
verses.19: And now, send over all of Israel to Mount Carmel. Also, send the prophets from the tribe of Benjamin—four thousand in total. And also send the prophets from the tribe of Asher—four thousand in total. They will be the ones who will eat the provisions that were prepared for them.
verses.20: And Ahahab sent out all the sons of Israel. He summoned the prophets to Mount Carmel.
verses.21: And he went to all the people and said, “Until I die, you will remain faithful to those two men. If Jehovah God leads them, then they shall go ahead of him. And if the man leads them, then they shall go ahead of him. But if the people do not respond to his words, then…”
verses.22: And Eliyahhu said to the people, “I will be the only prophet of Jehovah. There are four hundred and fifty prophets who serve as his messengers.”
verses.23: And they will give us two fruits. We will choose one of them, plant it in the trees, and no fire will be set to those trees. I will plant that fruit in the trees, and no fire will be lit there.
verses.24: And you call them by the name of your gods. But I will call them by the name of Jehovah. And that God who answers through fire is indeed the true God. He answered to all the people. They said, “This is good counsel.”
verses.25: And Elisha said to the prophets: “Choose one of these grains for yourselves. Then, since you are many, call upon your gods’ names. But do not set fire to it.”
verses.26: And they took the fruit that he had given them. They made it into bread, and they called out to the man’s name from morning till noon, saying, “Master, we have no answer. There is no sound or response.” Then they broke the altar that he had made.
verses.27: And it was in the evening, and Elijah stood among them. He said, “Cry out loudly, for this is God; he is the one who will come to them. He will lead them along the path they must take.”
verses.28: And they cried out loudly, and they were punished according to their crimes in the disasters and atrocities that took place upon them.
verses.29: And as the day began to fade away, they went up to the place where the offering was placed. There was no sound, no response, and no one was there to greet them.
verses.30: And Elijah said to all the people, “Come to me.” And all the people came to him. He then repaired the altar of Jehovah on Mount Ebal.
verses.31: And Elia took twelve stones, according to the number of the descendants of Jacob. This was a command from Jehovah to him: “Israel shall have your name.”
verses.32: And he built the stones from the stones used for the altar. He made a path around the altar, just like in the house of Satan.
verses.33: And he cut down the trees, and he planted the seeds in their places.
verses.34: And he said, “Fill four containers with water. Then pour it over the trees and the ground.” He also said, “Turn them around.” And they did turn them around. He also said, “Make seven of them.” And they indeed made seven of them.
verses.35: And the waters flowed around the altar, and also along the river, which was filled with water.
verses.36: And it happened during the days of the offering of the sacrifice. The prophet Elijah came to me and said, “The LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, says that today people will know that you are indeed the God of Israel. I am your servant, and by your word I have done all these things.”
verses.37: O LORD, help me! Let this people know that You are indeed the LORD God, and that You have filled their hearts with love.
verses.38: And the fire of Jehovah fell, and it consumed the trees, the stones, the rocks, and even the water that was in the valley.
verses.39: And all the people saw this, and they fell down before him. They said, “This is the God of Israel! This is the Lord!”
verses.40: And Elijah said to them, “Kill the prophets of the LORD. Do not let any of them escape alive. Then he took them and brought them to the river Kishon, and there he slaughtered them there.
verses.41: And He said to Elijah, “Go and eat and drink, for the time of the famine has come.”
verses.42: And Ahava went to eat and drink. Eliyah went up to the top of the citadel. He covered his face with his hands.
verses.43: And he said to the young man, “Please look out at the sea.” He stood up, looked out, and said, “There’s nothing there.” Then he said, “Return back seven times.”
verses.44: And it happened on the seventh day. He said, “Look! There’s a small boat like the size of a man’s hand coming up from the sea.” He said to Ehab, “Stop! Do not stop them from going forward.”
verses.45: And it continued like this, and the skies became thick with clouds. There was also a great flood. Ahab rushed forward, and Yizraela went along with him.
verses.46: And the hand of Jehovah was upon Eliyahou. He stripped off his clothes and rushed forward before Ahau, until he reached Yizreelah.
